{"summary":"Vaccines do not cause autism. Multiple large, high-quality studies and reviews by health organizations worldwide have demonstrated that there is no link between vaccines and autism spectrum disorder (ASD).cdc+2​
Scientific Evidence
Extensive research has examined claims linking the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine to autism, including the ingredients in vaccines such as thimerosal. These claims originated from a small, flawed study published in 1998, which has since been retracted for scientific misconduct and fraud. Subsequent studies, involving hundreds of thousands of children in multiple countries, have consistently found no difference in autism rates between vaccinated and unvaccinated children.chop+4​
Expert Consensus
Major medical organizations such as the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), and the National Academy of Medicine all state unequivocally that vaccines are safe and do not cause autism. No vaccine ingredient—including thimerosal—has been shown to contribute to ASD. These conclusions are based on decades of research and surveillance.aap+1​
Autism Causes
Autism has a complex set of causes, predominantly involving genetics, certain environmental influences during pregnancy, and other factors unrelated to vaccination. The increase in autism diagnoses over time is more likely explained by broader awareness, improved diagnostic criteria, and better screening—not vaccines.chop+1​
Why Misinformation Persists
Despite the clear scientific consensus, misinformation about vaccines and autism persists online, often due to outdated or disproven studies and anecdotal reports. These have been widely discredited by the medical community, and spreading such claims poses risks to public health and children’s wellbeing.kidshealth+2​
In summary, there is no credible evidence that vaccines cause autism in children or adults. Vaccines remain a safe and essential tool for protecting public health.cdc+2​","citations":["https://www.cdc.gov/vaccine-safety/about/autism.html","https://www.chop.edu/vaccine-education-center/vaccine-safety/vaccines-and-other-conditions/autism","https://www.aap.org/en/news-room/fact-checked/fact-checked-vaccines-safe-and-effect-no-link-to-autism/","https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/autism-studies.html"],"extractionConfidence":1,"extractionWarnings":[]}
